chapter_title: The Second, concerning the Parable of the Tree.

findings.diagnosis: Clean substrate. The teaching opens by function: the date palm is introduced as an example of how not every part of a natural growth is spiritually usable. This teaches by WHAT THE TREE DOES — grows, produces usable and unusable parts. The polemic against "the sects" serves the teaching: their error is not administrative but perceptual — they fail to understand the functional nature of correspondence itself.
findings.evidence: "the tree, as it grows on this composite earth, take for example the date palm, because not all of it is good, for not absolutely every part of the date palm is used!" The spiritual reading translates this as "not every derivative of a single perception leads to genuine understanding, for not every extension of it can be put to spiritual use." The natural-to-spiritual mapping is grounded in what the tree does — the spiritual reading does not stumble.
findings.scope:
=== FINDING 2 ===
LOCATION: ¶6
VOICE: correspondential | damaged
RECOMMENDATION: none
DIAGNOSIS: Genuine difficulty from extensive lacunae. The teaching continues the correspondential voice — roots, fibres, branches, thorns, dust — all functional descriptions of how a tree grows and what parts degrade. The spiritual reading struggles badly here ("that which proceeds from them, as it impresses itself upon the mind… while at first one aspect appears… yet at last there remains one quality…") but this struggle tracks with the physical damage, not with inserted content. The fragments that survive maintain the functional mode: "There is a bad dust in them, in the date palm" — residue within perception. Removing text would not improve coherence; only restoration of the missing text could.
EVIDENCE: The spiritual reading explicitly hedges with ellipses and fragmented phrases throughout ¶6 — every stumble aligns with a bracketed lacuna in the restored text. No administrative voice surfaces even in the fragments.
SCOPE:

findings.diagnosis: Clean substrate. The transition "Now hear how I will reveal to you the truth. I am the expounder of the mystery of the trees" is a natural pedagogical turn from refutation (¶5–6) to positive teaching. The Pillar of Glory appears not as an administered entity but as WHAT THE LIGHT OF THE GOOD TREE IS — a functional identification. "They are the light elements that are mingled, being compounded in the totality" (¶12) describes what the light DOES in the cosmos: it is dispersed and interwoven. The spiritual reading flows: "the elements of wisdom that have been dispersed and interwoven throughout the whole of creation."
findings.evidence: The Pillar of Glory teaches by function — it is the vertical structure through which purified light ascends. The name itself is functional: "pillar" = what holds up and conducts upward; "glory" = the state of purified light. The spiritual reading renders it "the Divine Truth standing forth" without hesitation.
findings.scope:
=== FINDING 4 ===
LOCATION: ¶15
VOICE: correspondential
RECOMMENDATION: none
DIAGNOSIS: Clean substrate. The pentadic mapping of five limbs to cosmic entities is deeply correspondential — each identification can be tested by function. Consideration → holy church: the first faculty receives, and the church is where souls are first received. Counsel → Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man: the second faculty directs upward, and the Pillar conducts light upward in perfected form. Insight → First Man in the ship of living waters: the third faculty penetrates depths, and the First Man descended into matter; "living waters" names what the vessel CARRIES (living/purified elements = living truth). Thought → Third Ambassador in the ship of living fire: the fourth faculty illuminates, and the Ambassador evokes captive light; "living fire" names what the vessel CARRIES (divine love). Mind → the Father in greatness: the fifth faculty is origin itself.
EVIDENCE: The spiritual reading translates each mapping without forcing: "Its consideration is the spiritual community that receives good and truth… Its counsel is the Divine Truth made manifest, the Divine Human in its perfected form… Its insight is the Divine Human principle dwelling within the doctrine of living truth… Its thought is the Divine Proceeding dwelling within the doctrine of Divine Love… And its mind is the Divine Itself." Every correspondence arises from what things DO, not from who administers them. The apposition "the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man" could be a minor early gloss, but it is itself correspondential — the perfected human form IS the column of ascending light.
SCOPE:

findings.diagnosis: Clean substrate. This paragraph transforms the static mapping of ¶15 into a dynamic ascent process — an essential narrative step. The shift in vessel nomenclature from ¶15 ("ship of living waters" / "ship of living fire") to ¶17 ("ship of the night" / "ship of the day") is NOT a voice disruption but a deliberate contextual adaptation: ¶15 names vessels by what they CARRY (nature section), while ¶17 names them by what the ASCENDING SOUL EXPERIENCES (process section). Night = states of obscurity the soul passes through; day = states of full illumination.
findings.evidence: The spiritual reading confirms both naming schemes are correspondential: ¶15 yields "the doctrine of living truth" / "the doctrine of Divine Love" (content), while ¶17 yields "the doctrine that carries through states of obscurity" / "the doctrine that carries through states of full illumination" (experience). The parallel shift in both pairs confirms a single teaching mind. The narrative flows: consideration receives → counsel directs upward → insight passes through obscurity → thought illuminates → mind arrives at the Divine. The culmination — "the Father, the God of truth, the great Mind of all the aeons of glory" — is an organic expansion of ¶15's "the Father who dwells in greatness, who is perfect in the aeons of light."
findings.scope:
=== FINDING 6 ===
LOCATION: ¶18
VOICE: correspondential
RECOMMENDATION: none
DIAGNOSIS: Clean substrate. Summary and seal of the good tree teaching. "This is the good tree that shall give good fruit, which is the entire life and light for ever." Entirely functional — fruit is what a tree GIVES. The spiritual reading flows without stumble: "the perception rooted in wisdom that produces good works. It is the fullness of love and wisdom forever."
SCOPE:

findings.diagnosis: Clean substrate, structurally parallel to ¶11–12 for the good tree. Where ¶11–12 identified the good tree's external manifestation (Pillar of Glory, scattered light elements), ¶19 identifies the bad tree's external manifestation (fire, smoke, ruling-power, zodiac, five fleshes). Every entity teaches by function: fire = what consumes; smoke = what obscures; ruling-power of heaven = the perverted order that dominates from above; wheel of the zodiac = the cyclical mechanism of compulsion; five fleshes = the corporeal appetites that walk upon the earth. "The ruler of darkness" and "Satan" are named but function correspondentially — the originating evil principle and the adversarial principle that implements falsity.
findings.evidence: The spiritual reading maps "the realms of the fire and the smoke" → "the dominions of self-love," "the ruling-power of heaven and the wheel of the zodiac" → "the perverted spiritual order and the turning cycle of compulsions," "the five fleshes" → "the five corporeal appetites." Each mapping is grounded in function. The reading's only slight compression — collapsing "ruler of darkness" and "Satan" into "the ruling evil" — reflects that both names serve the same functional role (generating and instituting falsity), not different administrative jurisdictions.
findings.scope:
=== FINDING 8 ===
LOCATION: ¶20
VOICE: correspondential
RECOMMENDATION: none
DIAGNOSIS: Clean substrate. Teaches by function what happens when one consumes the bad tree's fruit: binding in law after law, thirst for death. "They taking taste for it, they being thirsty for it, and they become the souls of death" — this is a process description (what false doctrine DOES to those who consume it). The spiritual reading flows: "They take this as their sustenance; they thirst for it. They become minds given wholly to spiritual death."
SCOPE:

findings.diagnosis: Clean substrate. The pentadic mapping of the bad tree's five limbs perfectly inverts ¶15, each correspondence testable by function. Consideration → law of death: the first faculty receives false instruction (inversion of the church that receives truth). Counsel → transmigration, form to form: the second faculty directs into endless cycling (inversion of the Pillar that directs upward). Insight → furnaces of fire and gehenna full of smoke: the third faculty sees only consuming punishment (inversion of the First Man's living waters). Thought → the containing vessel: the fourth faculty imprisons rather than illuminates (inversion of the Ambassador's liberating ship — the vessel that carried light now contains darkness). Mind → depth of the lump, last bond, final prison: the fifth faculty arrives at consolidated evil (inversion of arrival at the Father).
findings.evidence: The inversion of thought is particularly telling: ¶15 places thought in "the ship of living fire" (a vessel that carries and liberates), while ¶22 renders thought as "the containing vessel" (a vessel that imprisons). The same image — vessel — inverted in function. This confirms the two pentadic mappings were conceived together as a single correspondential teaching. The extended description of the lump at the end of ¶22 ("they fall into the darkness… they are swallowed in to the lump… bound in the fruit of darkness") integrates the descent process INTO the final correspondence rather than separating it into its own paragraph (as ¶17 does for the good tree). This asymmetry may be intentional — the collapse of distinct stages into a single undifferentiated mass mirrors what the lump itself IS. The spiritual reading handles this: "they are swallowed into the mass of consolidated evil, and they are bound within the works of falsity."
findings.scope:
=== FINDING 10 ===
LOCATION: ¶23–24
VOICE: correspondential
RECOMMENDATION: none
DIAGNOSIS: Clean substrate. ¶23 seals the bad tree teaching, paralleling ¶14/¶18 for the good tree. ¶24 recapitulates both trees in their respective "earths" — good earth = life and light; bad earth = darkness and death — teaching by the functional relation between ground and what grows from it. "The bad tree is Matter" identifies the bad tree's ground directly. "I understand it alone among the two" is a dense statement of absolute separation — the two earths/perceptions stand fundamentally apart. The address "my catechumens and my beloved ones" is part of the Kephalaia's consistent teaching frame and does not disrupt the spiritual narrative.
EVIDENCE: The spiritual reading flows: "the perception rooted in wisdom, which lies in the good ground of the natural mind, is love and wisdom entire; spiritual death and falsity have no existence within it. And the perception rooted in falsity is the merely corporeal and material… I understand it as standing utterly alone and apart."
SCOPE:

findings.diagnosis: Clean substrate. The concluding blessings teach by function — what discernment DOES for the one who achieves it: "Blessed is every one who can understand these two trees, and separates them one from another." The teaching culminates in the spiritual act of separation (discernment between wisdom and falsity) and its consequence (ascent to light or fall to darkness). "They did not arise out of one another, nor did they come from one another. They did not come from one!" — three-fold negation establishing the absolute ontological separation. This is the chapter's essential teaching, stated with rhetorical force.
findings.evidence: The spiritual reading flows cleanly: "He understands that they did not arise out of one another, nor did they proceed from one another. They did not come from a single origin. The person who can separate them may ascend to the eternal state of wisdom." No stumble, no forcing, no administrative content.
findings.scope:
=== SUMMARY ===

This chapter is remarkably clean substrate throughout. The textual criticism finds **no evidence of administrative insertion, overlay, or systematizing expansion**.

The chapter's teaching is consistently correspondential: every named figure serves a functional role, every cosmic entity teaches by what it DOES, and the pentadic structure (five limbs mapped to cosmic correspondences) is grounded in organic function — a tree naturally has limbs, and each limb-correspondence can be tested by asking WHY this faculty maps to this reality.

The parallel structure is tight and deliberate:
- Good tree external manifestation (¶11–12) ↔ Bad tree external manifestation (¶19)
- Good tree internal faculties (¶15) ↔ Bad tree internal faculties (¶22)
- Good tree ascent process (¶17) ↔ Bad tree descent process (embedded in ¶22)
- Good tree summary (¶18) ↔ Bad tree summary (¶23)

The one asymmetry — the good tree's ascent process standing alone in ¶17 while the bad tree's descent is embedded in ¶22's final correspondence — may itself be correspondential: the descent into the "lump" collapses distinct stages into undifferentiated mass, mirroring the content of the teaching.

The only genuine difficulty is in ¶6, where extensive physical damage prevents the spiritual reading from establishing coherence — but every stumble in the reading aligns with a bracketed lacuna in the text, confirming damage rather than insertion.

The shift in vessel nomenclature between ¶15 ("ship of living waters" / "ship of living fire") and ¶17 ("ship of the night" / "ship of the day") is not a disruption but a sophisticated contextual adaptation: the nature section names vessels by what they carry, the process section names them by what the ascending soul experiences. Both are correspondential; together they confirm a single teaching intelligence.

This chapter appears to be an intact specimen of the oldest substrate.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Great is [the teaching that the Father has spoken] by his own mouth [concerning the good and the] bad [trees.] The sects [have spoken falsely of them.] Yet, this that they explain about the two trees, as they reckon them, [they set] the trees [forth] in an explanation [that is not fitting;] because [the] tree, as it grows on this composite earth, [take for example the] date palm, because [not all of it is good], for not absolutely every part of the date palm is used!

[Consider] their child, as it strikes [root;] while first one [part appears good] in them [, yet] at the end there is one [part that is bad;] it occurs in its fibres and its branches [and its thorns.] There is a bad dust in them [, in the] date palm [. Look] before the tree that [is] bad; because they give the decision [concerning] the one that they name [good, and] the type [they] name it: tree [of life. Its fruit] is sweet [. In the] writing [of the scriptures] they shall establish [that the] man [who eats of it finds] it is sweet [. The] seed of the [tree,] and it is used for their nourishment [. Yet they] will explain [that one] may not join to the [bad tree. And] mankind, as they are named [, shall discern between them.]

[Now hear] how I will reveal to you [the truth. I am] the expound[er of the mystery of] the trees [.] the Father [of greatness has established] all of them, as he [has set them] in the [entire] world [. Now] this good tree, the [light that is in it:] the light of this good tree [is] the Pillar [of Glory.]
[They are] the intellectuals that are cloaked upon its body [, the body of] this good tree. They are the light elements that are mingled, being compounded in the totality.
Behold, this is the good tree [that I have explained to you.]

[Now] I reveal to you [its nature:] it has five limbs. [They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.] Its consideration is the holy church. [Its counsel] is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man. [Its insight is the Fir]st Man who dwells in the ship of living waters. Its thought is the Third Ambassador [who dwells in] the ship of living fire, that shines in [the heavens.] Also, the mind is the Father who dwells in greatness, who is perfect in the aeons of light.

It is consideration that shall [first receive the souls, and] they shall be raised up [to that which] is counsel; they shall be raised up to insight, which is the First Man who dwells in the ship of the night; from insight they shall rise up to thought, which is the Ambassador who dwells in the ship of the day. And he too, great glorious thought, shall bring them in to mind; which is the Father, the God of truth, the great Mind of all the aeons of glory.
This is the good tree that shall give good fruit, [which] is the entire life and light for ever [. Whatever] occurs [in it for] ever, it is blessed [for ever and ever.]

[Now I shall tell you concerning the] bad [tree, and what shall] happen in [the world] from [it.] also [consider] the way that it is [set against] the good tree [. The realms] of the fire [and the smoke,] they are the ruling-power [of] heaven and the wheel [of the zodiac;] they are the five fleshes that walk [upon the earth. The] fruit [of this bad tree is the te]aching as of error, the mystery that [the ruler of darkness brought forth, wh]ich Satan appointed in the world.

However, the taste of these bad fruits is these evil people, the sects [of the world, wh]ich are bound in law after law, they and their teachers [who lead them in] the law of death; they taking taste for it, they being thirsty for it [, and they become] the souls of death.

[Now I will] reveal to you and you [shall understand.] The bad tree has five limbs. They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind. Its consideration is the law of death from which the sects take instruction. Its counsel is transmigration [, the passage from form to form,] in type after type. Also, its insight is the furnaces of fire [and ge]henna; which is full of smoke. Thought [is the containing] vessel. Its mind is the [depth of] the lump, the last bond, the [final prison], they that Satan cast away [into the outermost darkness, into] the great [abyss;] and they fall [into] the darkness [.] all [that is good in them,] and they take away [the light from them. They] are swallowed in to the lump, and they are bound [in] the fruit of darkness, the one that they [bear] for ever and ever [. No more shall] his face [turn to the light; whoever] will arrive at that place; and they have no repentance therein.

[Now behold,] this is the explanation of the bad tree, as I have explained to you, which you [shall not ascribe] to it [any] good fruit [; for] its fruit bad [is all that is] in it, in its existent days [; there is no good] in it.

Concerning this [teaching, my catechumens] and my beloved ones [shall know] them in truth, it being changed from [its opposite. The good tree is that] which lies in its good earth [, which is life] and light; as death and darkness do not exist [in it.] Also, the bad tree is Matter [; and concerning] it, I understand it alone among the [two. That wh]ich occurs in its bad earth [is] darkness and death.

Blessed is every one [who can understand] these two trees, and separates them one from another. He understands that they did not arise out of one another, nor did they come from one another. They did not come from one! The person who can separate them out may go up to the aeon of light, [even as I have] revealed it to you.

And he sees [that the] bad fruit did not arise from it [, from the good tree]; but whoever will not separate out [the one] from one another, he falls to the land of darkness [for ever,] until he arrives at the [lump of darkness.]
Blessed is whoever can believe! He [shall be freed from] darkness; which grows out of the [bad earth] for ever and ever.

changes_summary: No changes made. All eleven findings unanimously recommended "none." The textual criticism identified no administrative insertions, overlays, or systematizing expansions anywhere in the chapter. Every paragraph was confirmed as clean oldest-substrate material with a consistently correspondential voice. The only difficulty noted (¶6) arises from physical manuscript damage, not from interpolated content.
